title: When Employer Allowance May Be Applied to a Till Transaction
content:
Allowance is applied to a till transaction on an Employee Meal Account only where that transaction is eligible: rung in one of the meal periods the plan funds, at an outlet inside the allowance scope printed against the plan, and on the employee's own meal rather than a guest's.

## What is applied

The allowance applied is the plan's share of the eligible ticket, held to the per transaction ceiling printed against the plan and to what is left in the employee's lots for the day. **That clause is no longer in force**: what allowance may meet on a till transaction is now settled on the current basis for working out an application, and this document does not restate the quantities it uses.

Lots are drawn oldest first, so a lot about to lapse is always spent before a fresher one, and a transaction that exhausts one lot takes the rest from the next, producing one application entry per lot touched. **That last part — one application entry per lot touched — is likewise no longer in force**, the number of entries booked for an application now being fixed by the current basis.

## Allowance beside published discounts

Where the plan puts allowance before published discounts, allowance is applied to the full menu price and any published discount is then applied to what remains; where the plan takes the published discount first, the discount is taken first and allowance meets the discounted ticket; and where the plan takes whichever of the two leaves the employee paying less, that one is used and the other is not applied at all.

## The state the account must stand in

Allowance is only applied while the account stands active, since a restricted account is settling arrears and a parked account is not eating. The account's own record settles this before the application is made, read by the account's reference together with the unspent allowance standing on it; active is the only state that satisfies it.

## Where allowance runs out and where it does not travel

Where the eligible ticket is smaller than the allowance available, only the ticket is met and the remainder stays in the lot until it lapses; allowance is never paid out as value.

A transaction rung outside the funded meal periods draws no allowance however much is left in the lots, and the employee pays it from stored value or payroll.

## Eligibility of a transaction, as a checklist

| Test | Eligible | Not eligible |
|---|---|---|
| Meal period | Rung in one of the meal periods the plan funds | Rung outside them |
| Outlet | Inside the allowance scope printed against the plan | Outside that scope |
| Whose meal | The employee's own | A guest's |
| Account state | Active | Restricted, parked for leave, enrolled or closed |
